     8	/-!
     9	# The widened adaptation and certificate (R2, human decision I-0492)
    10	
    11	`DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean` carries the widened cover datum `AffCoverData` — arbitrary
    12	affine opens, jointly covering, no chart typing.  This file puts the adaptation and the
    13	colength certificate on top of it, clause for clause as in `DivisorFamily.lean`:
    14	
    15	* `AffAdaptation` — equations `f_j` on the pieces plus the point-free refinement clause
    16	  `eqn_rel` (so it pulls back along arbitrary morphisms);
    17	* `colength`, `ovlColength`, `deltaLeft`/`deltaRight`, `gluedSubmodule` as a kernel;
    18	* `IsCertified` with (c1)–(c4) unchanged.
    19	
    20	**No clause is added and none is dropped.**  That is the point: consumers of the
    21	*certificate* port by reindexing alone.  What does not survive is the (β2) upgrade from
    22	"inside one piece" to "inside one chart" (`subset_chart₀_or_disjoint_chart₀` and
    23	`supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected`) — that upgrade is the no-go, not a tool, and
    24	nothing here may depend on it.
    25	
    26	The two facts the certificate layer actually uses about a piece are openness (for the
    27	clopen-trace/swallow-or-miss argument, `DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean`) and affineness (for
    28	(c1)-finiteness and the localization presentation).  Both are fields of `AffCoverData`, so
    29	the whole per-piece layer transports.
    30	
    31	## Main declarations
    32	
    33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation` — the widened adaptation.
    34	* `AffAdaptation.ofAnchors` — the anchored constructor (mirrors
    35	  `DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors`).
    36	* `AffAdaptation.eqn_regular` — the equations are regular, derived not stored.
    37	* `AffAdaptation.gluedSubmodule`, `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff` — the equalizer `W(d)`.
    38	* `AffAdaptation.IsCertified` — (c1)–(c4).
    39	* `AffAdaptation.subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus`,
    40	  `flat_colength_of_piece`, and the swallow-or-miss transport lemmas — the per-piece layer,
    41	  proved from openness and affineness only.
    42	-/

    45	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    46	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

    48	universe u

    50	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
    51	
    52	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

    54	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    55	
    56	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    57	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    58	
    59	/-- Restriction along `W ≤ V ≤ U` composes (the `private res_res` of
    60	`Picard/DivisorFamily.lean`, restated here because that one is file-private). -/
    61	private lemma res_res' {X : Scheme.{u}} {W V U : X.Opens} (h₁ : W ≤ V) (h₂ : V ≤ U)
    62	    (s : Γ(X, U)) :
    63	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₁).op).hom ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₂).op).hom s)
    64	      = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁.trans h₂)).op).hom s := by
    65	  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
    66	
    67	/-! ## The widened adaptation -/
    68	
    69	/-- **The adaptation of a local-equation system to a widened cover.** Identical in content to
    70	`DivisorAdaptation` except that the cover datum is an `AffCoverData`: equations on the pieces,
    71	plus the point-free pointwise refinement clause `eqn_rel`.
    72	
    73	`eqn_rel` quantifies over ALL `y` — on an empty overlap the section ring is the zero ring and
    74	the clause is trivial — which is what makes it pull back along arbitrary morphisms. -/
    75	structure AffAdaptation (D : AffCoverData C R) (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
    76	    Type u where
    77	  /-- The equation on the piece `j`. -/
    78	  eqn : ∀ j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)
    79	  /-- The equations refine `d` pointwise up to units. -/
    80	  eqn_rel : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C R),
    81	    ∃ u : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ,
    82	      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
    83	        = (u : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
    84	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y)
    85	
    86	namespace AffAdaptation
    87	
    88	variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    89	variable (A : AffAdaptation D d)
    90	
    91	/-- The index of the adaptation is the index of its cover. -/
    92	abbrev index : Type := D.index
    93	
    94	/-- **The anchored constructor.** A base point `pt j` of `d.cover` per piece with
    95	`pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j)` and a comparison unit; `eqn_rel` is derived by transporting
    96	`d.eqn (pt j)` to `d.eqn y` through `d.ratioUnit`, exactly as in
    97	`DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors`. -/
    98	def ofAnchors
    99	    (eqn : ∀ j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
   100	    (pt : D.index → relCurve C R)
   101	    (piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j))
   102	    (unit : ∀ j, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)ˣ)
   103	    (eqn_eq : ∀ j, eqn j = (unit j : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
   104	      * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (piece_le j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j))) :
   105	    AffAdaptation D d where
   106	  eqn := eqn
   107	  eqn_rel := fun j y => by
   108	    have hWle : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
   109	        ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y :=
   110	      inf_le_inf (piece_le j) le_rfl
   111	    have E1 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
   112	      (inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (eqn_eq j)
   113	    rw [map_mul, res_res'] at E1
   114	    have E2 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE hWle).op).hom
   115	      (d.eqn_restrict_eq (pt j) y)
   116	    rw [map_mul, res_res', res_res'] at E2
   117	    refine ⟨(relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)
   118	      * (relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y), ?_⟩
   119	    rw [Units.val_mul]
   120	    calc ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
   121	        = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
   122	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
   123	              ((inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j).trans
   124	                (piece_le j))).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)) := by
   125	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
   126	              D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j) (unit j)).val
   127	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
   128	                  D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (unit j).val
   129	            from rfl]
   130	          exact E1
   131	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
   132	          * (((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
   133	            * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (hWle.trans
   134	                (inf_le_right : d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y
   135	                  ≤ d.cover.opens y))).op).hom (d.eqn y)) := by
   136	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
   137	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
   138	                  (homOfLE hWle).op).hom (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y).val from rfl]
   139	          rw [E2]
   140	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
   141	          * ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
   142	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
   143	              (inf_le_right : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
   144	                ≤ d.cover.opens y)).op).hom (d.eqn y) := by
   145	          rw [mul_assoc]

   147	/-- **The equations are regular** — derived from `eqn_rel` at the point itself, not stored. -/
   148	theorem eqn_regular (j : D.index) (z : relCurve C R) (hz : z ∈ D.pieces j) :
   149	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
   150	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
   151	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j z
   152	  have hzW : z ∈ D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z := ⟨hz, d.cover.mem_opens z⟩
   153	  have hgerm : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
   154	      = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom
   155	          (u : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z))
   156	        * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens z) z
   157	            (d.cover.mem_opens z)).hom (d.eqn z) := by
   158	    have h := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   159	      (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom hu
   160	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
   161	    exact h
   162	  rw [hgerm]
   163	  exact mul_mem
   164	    ((u.isUnit.map ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   165	      (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom).mem_nonZeroDivisors)
   166	    (d.regular z z (d.cover.mem_opens z))
   167	
   168	/-! ### The colength modules and the glued equalizer -/
   169	
   170	/-- The piece-local colength module `Γ(pieces j) ⧸ (f_j)`. -/
   171	noncomputable abbrev colength (j : D.index) : Type u :=
   172	  Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) ⧸ Ideal.span {A.eqn j}
   173	
   174	/-- The symmetric overlap ideal, generated by both restricted equations. -/
   175	noncomputable abbrev ovlIdeal (i j : D.index) :
   176	    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) :=
   177	  Ideal.span
   178	    {relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i) (A.eqn i),
   179	     relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces j) (A.eqn j)}
   180	
   181	/-- The overlap colength module. -/
   182	noncomputable abbrev ovlColength (i j : D.index) : Type u :=
   183	  Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) ⧸ A.ovlIdeal i j
   184	
   185	/-- Restrict-then-quotient, from the `i` component. -/
   186	noncomputable def toOvlLeft (i j : D.index) : A.colength i →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
   187	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn i})
   188	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_left))
   189	    (by
   190	      intro a ha
   191	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
   192	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
   193	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
   194	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
   195	          (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i) (A.eqn i)
   196	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
   197	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)
   198	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
   199	
   200	/-- Restrict-then-quotient, from the `j` component. -/
   201	noncomputable def toOvlRight (i j : D.index) : A.colength j →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
   202	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
   203	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_right))
   204	    (by
   205	      intro a ha
   206	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
   207	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
   208	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
   209	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
   210	          (inf_le_right : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces j) (A.eqn j)
   211	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
   212	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ rfl)
   213	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
   214	
   215	/-- The product of the piece-local colengths. -/
   216	noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : D.index, A.colength j
   217	
   218	/-- The product of the overlap colengths over ordered index pairs. -/
   219	noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : D.index × D.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2
   220	
   221	/-- The left arrow of the equalizer. -/
   222	noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   223	  LinearMap.pi
   224	    (fun p : D.index × D.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)
   225	
   226	/-- The right arrow of the equalizer. -/
   227	noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   228	  LinearMap.pi
   229	    (fun p : D.index × D.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
   230	
   231	/-- **The glued colength module `W(d)`**, spelled as a kernel so the `FlatCokernel`
   232	base-change keystone applies verbatim. -/
   233	noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
   234	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)
   235	
   236	/-- The equalizer description of `W(d)`. -/
   237	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
   238	    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : D.index × D.index,
   239	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
   240	  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
   241	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   242	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]
   243	
   244	/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/
   245	noncomputable abbrev Glued : Type u := ↥A.gluedSubmodule
   246	
   247	/-! ### The certificate -/
   248	
   249	/-- **The colength certificate over a widened cover** — clauses (c1)–(c4) verbatim from
   250	`DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified`.  Nothing is added and nothing is dropped: the widening
   251	changes where the pieces LIVE, not what the certificate asserts. -/
   252	structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
   253	  /-- (c1) Each piece-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
   254	  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
   255	  /-- (c1) Each piece-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
   256	  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
   257	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
   258	  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
   259	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
   260	  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
   261	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
   262	  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
   263	  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
   264	  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
   265	  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
   266	  flat_coker_diff :
   267	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
   268	
   269	end AffAdaptation
   270	
   271	end AlgebraicGeometry

     8	/-!
     9	# Widened-adaptation extraction (R2, human decision I-0492)
    10	
    11	**Every** local-equation system on the relative curve refines to a widened adaptation, with no
    12	chart input whatsoever: `AffAdaptation.exists` below is the R2 counterpart of
    13	`exists_divisorAdaptation` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyExtraction.lean`).
    14	
    15	## Why this is the shape the widening was for
    16	
    17	The chart-typed extraction runs the affine-refinement engine **on each of the two pinned
    18	charts** and glues the results with a partition of unity per chart — the partitions are what
    19	`exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement` produces, and they are exactly what protection I-0492
    20	ordered deleted.  Here there is nothing to glue: affine opens form a basis of any scheme
    21	(`Scheme.isBasis_affineOpens`), the relative curve is quasi-compact when `C` is (being a base
    22	change of `C.left`), so one pass gives a finite affine-open cover subordinated to `d.cover`.
    23	No `π`, no charts, no partitions, no `Sum` index.
    24	
    25	The comparison unit is `1` at every piece, as in the chart-typed extraction: the equation is
    26	literally the restriction of `d`'s equation at the anchor.
    27	
    28	## Main declarations
    29	
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instQuasiCompactRelCurveHom`, `instCompactSpaceRelCurve` — the relative
    31	  curve over a proper `C` is quasi-compact over its test base, hence compact.
    32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affCoverData_subordinate` — a finite affine-open cover with, per
    33	  piece, an anchor point of `d.cover` whose member contains the piece.
    34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affAdaptation` — hence a widened adaptation of `d`.
    35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affAdaptation_of_isProper` — the same with the compactness
    36	  hypothesis discharged, so with NO hypothesis on the system.
    37	
    38	## What this does and does not close
    39	
    40	It closes the *adaptation* half of the widened lane's producer gap: before this file, the only
    41	way to obtain an `AffAdaptation` was `FinCoverData.toAffCoverData` plus
    42	`DivisorAdaptation.toAff` — i.e. through the chart-typed predicate, which is exactly the route
    43	R2 exists to avoid.  Now a widened adaptation exists for every system, directly.
    44	
    45	It does NOT produce a *certificate*.  The two obligations protection I-0492 clause 4 relocated
    46	— fibrewise-finite support and `SwallowedBy` — remain obligations, and a cover produced by this
    47	extraction has no reason to have a straddling piece.  Producing one that does is where the
    48	Stacks `0B8B` input enters, and that is still owed.
    49	-/
    50	
    51	set_option autoImplicit false
    52	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    53	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    54	
    55	universe u
    56	
    57	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
    58	
    59	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    60	
    61	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    62	
    63	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    64	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    65	
    66	/-- **The relative curve over a proper `C` is quasi-compact over its test base.**  `IsProper`
    67	implies `QuasiCompact`, and quasi-compactness is stable under base change along
    68	`Over.isPullback_left`. -/
    69	instance instQuasiCompactRelCurveHom [IsProper C.hom] :
    70	    QuasiCompact (relCurve C R ↘ Spec (.of R)) :=
    71	  MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @QuasiCompact)
    72	    (Over.isPullback_left C (overSpec k R)) inferInstance
    73	
    74	/-- **The relative curve over a proper `C` has a compact space.**  `Spec R` is compact and the
    75	structure morphism is quasi-compact, so this is
    76	`QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace`.
    77	
    78	This is what makes the extraction below hypothesis-free in the case of interest: the finite
    79	subcover it extracts exists because the curve is quasi-compact, and nothing else about it
    80	matters. -/
    81	instance instCompactSpaceRelCurve [IsProper C.hom] : CompactSpace (relCurve C R) :=

    14	
    15	> **READ `isEmpty_chartTyping_of_straddling` (below) BEFORE THIS DOCSTRING'S ARGUMENT.**
    16	> This module's original headline was "the widened carrier had no Θ-layer, and supplying it lets
    17	> cert-r2's producer reach U2". **The first clause is true; the second is refuted, in Lean, in
    18	> this file.** Every declaration here is indexed by a `ChartTyping C R π D`, and a cover with a
    19	> straddling piece admits *none* — which is exactly the case protection `I-0492`'s widening
    20	> exists to handle. So on those divisors every theorem below is vacuous, and the tree's only

    24	> What survives is worth keeping and is not the headline: the Θ-layer genuinely did not exist on
    25	> `AffAdaptation` (measurements below, independently confirmed as `I-0780`), it ports cleanly, and

    27	
    28	Protection `I-0492` widened the certificate carrier to arbitrary affine opens, and the

    36	## The measurement that renames the seam
    37	
    38	U2's consumer `DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause` (`Picard/DivRepAffPullClause.lean:121`)

    41	a straddling divisor has no chart-typed certificate).  So the only usable route is to

    43	
    44	> `divFamEps_eq_of_le` (`Picard/DivRepChartClassUnivQuot.lean`) needs projectivity and

    57	## Why this is a port and not new mathematics
    58	
    59	The Θ-layer's chart-dependence is exactly **one `Bool` per piece**.  `FinCoverData`'s
    60	version reads it off the `Sum` index (`pieces_inl_le` / `pieces_inr_le`), which is why it

    64	* `relThetaResSide` (`Picard/DivSchemeFamilySide.lean:155`) — the side component,

    66	* `relThetaSideUnit` (`:180`) — the matching unit of an ordered pair of sides, whose

    68	* `relThetaResSide_matching` (`:194`) and `resHom_relThetaResSide` (`:172`).

    74	
    75	So this file is the missing face, built the way clause 3 intends: the twisting data is

    79	## What this file does and does not claim
    80

    86	It does **not** prove surjectivity of the widened evaluation (the right-exactness heart,

   100	  `H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ)) → W(d)^{Θᵃ}`.
   101	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation.ker_thetaGluedEval` — **the kernel bridge**: the widened
   102	  kernel *is* the cover-independent vanishing submodule, hence literally the chart-typed
   103	  layer's kernel.
   104	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation.windowCarve` / `ker_windowCarve` / `windowQuotEquiv` — the
   105	  bridge plugged in: the widened carve arrow's kernel is `divisorWindow d`, and (conditional on
   106	  surjectivity, which is **not** proved here) the quotient of the free window by it is the
   107	  widened `W(d)^{Θᵃ}`.  That last equivalence is the vehicle whose absence made the ε-value at a
   108	  `DivFamZarAff` unstateable.
   109	
   110	**A phrasing correction taken from a fresh-context review** (`I-0769`), because the wrong version
   111	was in this docstring: `ker_thetaGluedEval` does **not** show "`divisorWindow` is the same on both
   112	carriers" — `divisorWindow` takes only `d` and `hH1` and never mentioned a carrier, so that is
   113	vacuous.  The content runs the other way: *the widened evaluation's kernel lands on that
   114	already-fixed submodule.*
   115	-/

   132	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   133	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
   134	/- `ChartTyping` is stated with an `[IsAffineHom π]` binder, which `[IsFinite π]` already
   135	supplies — the `overlappingInstances` linter reports the pair, so only `IsFinite` is taken
   136	here and `IsAffineHom` is found by synthesis. -/
   137	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]

   139	namespace AffAdaptation
   140	
   141	variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
   142	variable (A : AffAdaptation D d) (τ : ChartTyping C R π D) (a : ℕ)
   143	
   144	/-! ## The twisting unit, read off a chart typing
   145	
   146	`FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyTheta.lean:149`) splits on the `Sum`
   147	index and produces `1`, the cocycle, or its inverse.  That is `relThetaSideUnit` at the two
   148	pieces' sides, and here the sides come from `τ` rather than from the index type — which is
   149	the whole difference between the two layers. -/
   150	
   151	/-- The pinned chart assigned to a widened piece agrees with `relPinnedChart` on the nose
   152	(`pinnedChartOfSide` is `bif`, `relPinnedChart` is a match on the same `Bool`). -/
   153	lemma pinnedChartOfSide_eq (b : Bool) :
   154	    pinnedChartOfSide C R π b = relPinnedChart C R π b := by
   155	  cases b <;> rfl
   156	
   157	/-- The piece is contained in the pinned chart of its assigned side, in the
   158	`relPinnedChart` spelling the side-uniform Θ API consumes. -/
   159	lemma piece_le_relPinnedChart (j : D.index) :
   160	    D.pieces j ≤ relPinnedChart C R π (τ.side j) :=
   161	  (pinnedChartOfSide_eq (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) (τ.side j)) ▸ τ.piece_le j
   162	
   163	/-- An overlap of two widened pieces sits below both assigned pinned charts. -/
   164	lemma pieces_inf_le_relPinnedChart_inf (i j : D.index) :
   165	    D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j
   166	      ≤ relPinnedChart C R π (τ.side i) ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π (τ.side j) :=
   167	  inf_le_inf (piece_le_relPinnedChart τ i) (piece_le_relPinnedChart τ j)
   168	
   169	/-- **The Θ twisting unit of an ordered pair of widened pieces**: the side matching unit
   170	of the two assigned sides, restricted to the overlap.  This replaces
   171	`FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit`'s four-case `Sum` split by one application of
   172	`relThetaSideUnit` — the cases are the same cases, and the `Bool`s now come from the
   173	separate `ChartTyping` datum rather than from the index type. -/
   174	noncomputable def thetaOvlUnit (i j : D.index) :
   175	    Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)ˣ :=
   176	  relThetaSideUnit a (τ.side i) (τ.side j) (pieces_inf_le_relPinnedChart_inf τ i j)
   177	
   178	/-- **The side matching unit at exponent `0` is trivial**, for any pair of sides.  The
   179	side-uniform form of `FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_zero` (`Picard/DivisorDatumInverse.lean:155`),
   180	whose four `Sum` cases are these four `Bool` cases.
   181	
   182	The split is over *variable* `Bool`s here (not over `τ.side j` at a use site), which is what
   183	keeps it out of the dependent-motive trap. -/
   184	lemma relThetaSideUnit_zero (b b' : Bool) {W : (relCurve C R).Opens}
   185	    (hW : W ≤ relPinnedChart C R π b ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π b') :
   186	    relThetaSideUnit (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) 0 b b' hW = 1 := by
   187	  cases b <;> cases b'
   188	  · rfl
   189	  · rw [show relThetaSideUnit (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) 0 false true hW
   190	        = (relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hW (relThetaCocycle C R π 0) from rfl,
   191	      relThetaCocycle_zero, map_one]
   192	  · rw [show relThetaSideUnit (C := C) (R := R) (π := π) 0 true false hW
   193	        = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict
   194	            (le_inf (hW.trans inf_le_right) (hW.trans inf_le_left))
   195	            (relThetaCocycle C R π 0))⁻¹ from rfl,
   196	      relThetaCocycle_zero, map_one, inv_one]
   197	  · rfl
   198	
   199	/-- The widened twisting unit is trivial at exponent `0`. -/
   200	lemma thetaOvlUnit_zero (i j : D.index) : thetaOvlUnit τ 0 i j = 1 :=
   201	  relThetaSideUnit_zero (τ.side i) (τ.side j) (pieces_inf_le_relPinnedChart_inf τ i j)
   202	
   203	/-! ## The Θ-twisted glued colength module -/
   204	
   205	/-- **The Θ-twisted right overlap arrow** over a widened cover: restrict the `p.2`
   206	component to each overlap and multiply by the twisting unit of the pair.  Verbatim
   207	`DivisorAdaptation.thetaDeltaRight` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyTheta.lean:203`) with
   208	`thetaOvlUnit` read off `τ`. -/
   209	noncomputable def thetaDeltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   210	  LinearMap.pi (fun p : D.index × D.index =>
   211	    LinearMap.mulLeft R (Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
   212	        ((thetaOvlUnit τ a p.1 p.2 :
   213	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   214	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))) ∘ₗ
   215	      (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
   216	
   217	/-- **The Θ-twisted glued colength module `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` over a widened cover**, spelled as a
   218	kernel so the `FlatCokernel` base-change shapes apply exactly as chart-typed. -/
   219	noncomputable def thetaGluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
   220	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - thetaDeltaRight A τ a)
   221	
   222	/-- The twisted-equalizer description of the widened `W(d)^{Θᵃ}`. -/
   223	lemma mem_thetaGluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
   224	    s ∈ thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a ↔ ∀ p : D.index × D.index,
   225	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1)
   226	        = Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
   227	            ((thetaOvlUnit τ a p.1 p.2 :
   228	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   229	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))
   230	          * A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
   231	  simp only [thetaGluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
   232	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, thetaDeltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   233	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply,
   234	    LinearMap.mulLeft_apply]
   235	
   236	/-- The widened Θ-twisted glued colength module, as a type. -/
   237	noncomputable abbrev ThetaGlued : Type u := ↥(thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a)
   238	
   239	/-! ## The evaluation `H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ)) → W(d)^{Θᵃ}` -/
   240	
   241	/-- **The germ of a widened equation spans the stalk ideal of the family.**  The widened
   242	counterpart of `DivisorAdaptation.germ_eqn_span_eq_stalkIdeal`
   243	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyTheta.lean:322`); its proof is the same one, and it ports because
   244	`eqn_rel` is stated pointwise on both carriers. -/
   245	theorem germ_eqn_span_eq_stalkIdeal (j : D.index) {z : relCurve C R}
   246	    (hz : z ∈ D.pieces j) :
   247	    Ideal.span {((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)}
   248	      = d.stalkIdeal z := by
   249	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j z
   250	  have hzW : z ∈ D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z := ⟨hz, d.cover.mem_opens z⟩
   251	  have hgerm : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
   252	      = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom
   253	          (u : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z))
   254	        * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens z) z
   255	            (d.cover.mem_opens z)).hom (d.eqn z) := by
   256	    have h := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   257	      (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom hu
   258	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
   259	    exact h
   260	  rw [hgerm, Ideal.span_singleton_mul_left_unit (u.isUnit.map
   261	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom)]
   262	  exact d.germ_eqn_span_eq z z (d.cover.mem_opens z)
   263	
   264	/-- The per-piece evaluation of a global theta section: take the side component assigned to
   265	the piece, restrict it, and reduce mod `(f_j)`.  Where the chart-typed version splits on the
   266	`Sum` index (`DivisorAdaptation.thetaPieceEval`), this is one application of
   267	`relThetaResSide` at `τ.side j`. -/
   268	noncomputable def thetaPieceEval (j : D.index) :
   269	    relThetaSections C R π a →ₗ[R] A.colength j :=
   270	  (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})).toLinearMap ∘ₗ
   271	    relThetaResSide a (τ.side j) (piece_le_relPinnedChart τ j)
   272	
   273	/-- **The section evaluation into the widened chart product.** -/
   274	noncomputable def thetaEval : relThetaSections C R π a →ₗ[R] A.chartProd :=
   275	  LinearMap.pi (thetaPieceEval A τ a)
   276	
   277	@[simp]
   278	lemma thetaEval_apply (x : relThetaSections C R π a) (j : D.index) :
   279	    thetaEval A τ a x j
   280	      = Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
   281	          (relThetaResSide a (τ.side j) (piece_le_relPinnedChart τ j) x) := rfl
   282	
   283	/-- The left overlap arrow on a residue class: restrict into the overlap, then reduce.
   284	
   285	Stated here because both widened forms exist only as `private` lemmas of
   286	`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffCert.lean` (`toOvlLeft_mk'`/`toOvlRight_mk'`) — and both are `rfl`,
   287	so this is a name, not a proof (inbox `I-0712`: `private` hides the name, not the argument).
   288	The `resHom` spelling is the one the matching law below rewrites along. -/
   289	lemma toOvlLeft_mk (i j : D.index) (s : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i)) :
   290	    A.toOvlLeft i j (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {A.eqn i}) s)
   291	      = Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal i j)
   292	          ((relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left s) :=
   293	  rfl
   294	
   295	/-- The right overlap arrow on a residue class. -/
   296	lemma toOvlRight_mk (i j : D.index) (s : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)) :
   297	    A.toOvlRight i j (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {A.eqn j}) s)
   298	      = Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal i j)
   299	          ((relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right s) :=
   300	  rfl
   301	
   302	/-- **The evaluation lands in the widened Θ-twisted glued module**: on each pairwise
   303	overlap, the global matching of the two side components through the theta cocycle *is* the
   304	Θ-twisted matching of the colengths.
   305	
   306	Where the chart-typed proof (`DivisorAdaptation.thetaEval_mem`) runs a four-case `Sum`
   307	split and calls `relThetaSections_matching` twice with hand-built containments, this is a
   308	single application of `relThetaResSide_matching` — the side-uniform form of the same
   309	matching law.  That collapse is the concrete payoff of taking the sides from a
   310	`ChartTyping` rather than from the index type. -/
   311	theorem thetaEval_mem (x : relThetaSections C R π a) :
   312	    thetaEval A τ a x ∈ thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a := by
   313	  rw [mem_thetaGluedSubmodule_iff]
   314	  rintro ⟨i, j⟩
   315	  rw [thetaEval_apply, thetaEval_apply, toOvlLeft_mk, toOvlRight_mk, ← map_mul]
   316	  refine congrArg _ ?_
   317	  -- both sides restrict the SAME section into the overlap; the side matching law compares
   318	  -- the two assigned sides there, and `thetaOvlUnit` is by definition its unit
   319	  rw [resHom_relThetaResSide (b := τ.side i), resHom_relThetaResSide (b := τ.side j)]
   320	  exact relThetaResSide_matching a (τ.side i) (τ.side j)
   321	    (pieces_inf_le_relPinnedChart_inf τ i j) x
   322	
   323	/-- **The evaluation `H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ)) → W(d)^{Θᵃ}` over a widened cover.** -/
   324	noncomputable def thetaGluedEval :
   325	    relThetaSections C R π a →ₗ[R] ThetaGlued A τ a :=
   326	  LinearMap.codRestrict (thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a) (thetaEval A τ a) (thetaEval_mem A τ a)
   327	
   328	lemma thetaGluedEval_coe (x : relThetaSections C R π a) :
   329	    (thetaGluedEval A τ a x : A.chartProd) = thetaEval A τ a x := rfl
   330	
   331	/-- The kernel of the corestricted evaluation is the kernel of the evaluation. -/
   332	lemma ker_thetaGluedEval_eq_ker :
   333	    LinearMap.ker (thetaGluedEval A τ a) = LinearMap.ker (thetaEval A τ a) :=
   334	  LinearMap.ker_codRestrict _ _ _

   336	/-! ## The equalizer algebra and the unit-twisted glued modules
   337	
   338	Everything in this section is **cover-generic**: it names `D.pieces`, `A.ovlIdeal`,
   339	`A.toOvlLeft/Right` and nothing about a chart, so it ports from
   340	`Picard/DivisorFamilyThetaRank.lean:77-231` with `AffAdaptation` in place of
   341	`DivisorAdaptation` and no other change.  It is the substrate a widened `IsThetaPaired` —
   342	the honest cohomological residue of the (c2)-transport — is stated over. -/
   343	
   344	/-- **The equalizer algebra `A_D` over a widened cover**: the glued colength module is an
   345	`R`-subalgebra of the piece product, because the overlap-restriction arrows are algebra
   346	maps. -/
   347	noncomputable def gluedSubalgebra : Subalgebra R A.chartProd where
   348	  carrier := A.gluedSubmodule
   349	  add_mem' := fun hx hy => A.gluedSubmodule.add_mem hx hy
   350	  mul_mem' := by
   351	    intro x y hx hy
   352	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff] at hx hy ⊢
   353	    intro p
   354	    rw [Pi.mul_apply, Pi.mul_apply, map_mul, map_mul, hx p, hy p]
   355	  one_mem' := by
   356	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
   357	    intro p
   358	    rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, map_one, map_one]
   359	  algebraMap_mem' := by
   360	    intro r
   361	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
   362	    intro p
   363	    rw [Pi.algebraMap_apply, Pi.algebraMap_apply, AlgHom.commutes, AlgHom.commutes]
   364	
   365	lemma mem_gluedSubalgebra_iff {x : A.chartProd} :
   366	    x ∈ gluedSubalgebra A ↔ x ∈ A.gluedSubmodule :=
   367	  Iff.rfl
   368	
   369	/-- The equalizer algebra and the glued module have the same carrier, `R`-linearly. -/
   370	noncomputable def gluedSubalgebraEquiv : ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) ≃ₗ[R] A.Glued where
   371	  toFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
   372	  invFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
   373	  map_add' _ _ := rfl
   374	  map_smul' _ _ := rfl
   375	  left_inv _ := rfl
   376	  right_inv _ := rfl

   378	section UnitTwist
   379	
   380	variable (u v : ∀ i j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)ˣ)
   381	
   382	/-- The `u`-twisted right overlap arrow for an arbitrary unit family on the piece
   383	overlaps. -/
   384	noncomputable def unitDeltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   385	  LinearMap.pi (fun p : D.index × D.index =>
   386	    LinearMap.mulLeft R (Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
   387	        ((u p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   388	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))) ∘ₗ
   389	      (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
   390	
   391	/-- The `u`-twisted glued colength module. -/
   392	noncomputable def unitGluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
   393	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - unitDeltaRight A u)
   394	
   395	/-- The `u`-twisted equalizer description. -/
   396	lemma mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
   397	    s ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A u ↔ ∀ p : D.index × D.index,
   398	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1)
   399	        = Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
   400	            ((u p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   401	              Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))
   402	          * A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
   403	  simp only [unitGluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
   404	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, unitDeltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   405	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply,
   406	    LinearMap.mulLeft_apply]
   407	
   408	/-- At the trivial unit family, the twisted glued module is the glued module. -/
   409	lemma unitGluedSubmodule_one : unitGluedSubmodule A 1 = A.gluedSubmodule := by
   410	  ext s
   411	  rw [mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff, mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
   412	  refine forall_congr' fun p => ?_
   413	  rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, Units.val_one, map_one, one_mul]
   414	
   415	/-- At the Θ unit family, the twisted glued module is the widened `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` — by `rfl`,
   416	exactly as chart-typed, which is what lets the pairing layer be stated over `thetaOvlUnit`
   417	without a transport. -/
   418	lemma unitGluedSubmodule_thetaOvlUnit :
   419	    unitGluedSubmodule A (thetaOvlUnit τ a) = thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a :=
   420	  rfl
   421	
   422	variable {u v}
   423	
   424	/-- **Twists multiply**: the componentwise product of a `u`-twisted and a `v`-twisted glued
   425	family is `(u * v)`-twisted. -/
   426	theorem mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule {s t : A.chartProd}
   427	    (hs : s ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A u) (ht : t ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A v) :
   428	    s * t ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A (u * v) := by
   429	  rw [mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff] at hs ht ⊢
   430	  intro p
   431	  have h1 : (s * t) p.1 = s p.1 * t p.1 := rfl
   432	  have h2 : (s * t) p.2 = s p.2 * t p.2 := rfl
   433	  have h3 : (((u * v) p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   434	      Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))
   435	      = ((u p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   436	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))
   437	        * ((v p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
   438	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)) := rfl
   439	  rw [h1, h2, h3, map_mul, map_mul, map_mul, hs p, ht p]
   440	  ring
   441	
   442	variable (u) in
   443	/-- The `u`-twisted glued module as a module over the equalizer algebra `A_D`. -/
   444	noncomputable def unitGluedOver : Submodule ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) A.chartProd where
   445	  carrier := unitGluedSubmodule A u
   446	  add_mem' := fun hx hy => (unitGluedSubmodule A u).add_mem hx hy
   447	  zero_mem' := (unitGluedSubmodule A u).zero_mem
   448	  smul_mem' := by
   449	    intro c x hx
   450	    have hc : (c : A.chartProd) ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A 1 := by
   451	      rw [unitGluedSubmodule_one]
   452	      exact c.2
   453	    have hmul := mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule A hc hx
   454	    rw [one_mul] at hmul
   455	    have hsmul : c • x = (c : A.chartProd) * x := Algebra.smul_def c x
   456	    rw [SetLike.mem_coe, hsmul]
   457	    exact hmul
   458	
   459	lemma mem_unitGluedOver_iff {x : A.chartProd} :
   460	    x ∈ unitGluedOver A u ↔ x ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A u :=
   461	  Iff.rfl
   462

   532	/-- The widened `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` as an `A_D`-submodule. -/

   534	  unitGluedOver A (thetaOvlUnit τ a)

   536	/-- The widened inverse-twisted glued module as an `A_D`-submodule. -/

   538	  unitGluedOver A (thetaOvlUnit τ a)⁻¹

   541	    x ∈ thetaSpan A τ a ↔ x ∈ thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a :=
   542	  Iff.rfl

   544	lemma mem_thetaInvSpan_iff {x : A.chartProd} :

   546	  Iff.rfl

   548	/-- Products of `Θᵃ`- and `Θ⁻ᵃ`-sections are untwisted: the pairing lands in the equalizer

   551	    thetaSpan A τ a * thetaInvSpan A τ a ≤ 1 := by
   552	  rw [Submodule.mul_le]
   553	  intro s hs t ht
   554	  have hmul := mul_mem_unitGluedSubmodule A
   555	    (mem_thetaSpan_iff A τ a |>.mp hs) (mem_thetaInvSpan_iff A τ a |>.mp ht)
   556	  rw [mul_inv_cancel, unitGluedSubmodule_one] at hmul
   557	  rw [Submodule.one_eq_range]
   558	  exact ⟨⟨s * t, hmul⟩, rfl⟩
   559	
   560	/-- **The widened pairing input**: the `Θᵃ`- and `Θ⁻ᵃ`-twisted glued modules pair onto the
   561	full equalizer algebra.  Named so the remaining (c2)-transport obligation over the widened
   562	carrier is a *statement in the tree* rather than a gap in prose.
   563	
   564	**This is not proved here, and the reason is precise.** Chart-typed, it is discharged by
   565	`isThetaPaired_of_sectionWitness` from two manufactured global sections `σ = (t₀ᵃ, 1)`,
   566	`τ = (1, t₁ᵃ)` read through the **pinned chart trivializations** — that is where the fixed
   567	pair genuinely enters the Θ-layer, and nothing above needed it.  A widened witness must
   568	produce the analogous sections from the `ChartTyping` instead; whether the per-piece
   569	coordinates suffice is the open question. -/
   570	def IsThetaPaired : Prop :=
   571	  thetaSpan A τ a * thetaInvSpan A τ a = 1

   573	/-- The widened pairing input reduces to hitting `1`. -/
   574	theorem isThetaPaired_of_one_mem
   575	    (h : (1 : A.chartProd) ∈ thetaSpan A τ a * thetaInvSpan A τ a) :
   576	    IsThetaPaired A τ a := by
   577	  refine le_antisymm (thetaSpan_mul_thetaInvSpan_le_one A τ a) ?_

   581	/-! ### The satisfiability probe on `IsThetaPaired`
   582	
   583	`IsThetaPaired` is a `Prop` this file defines and does not prove, so per the standing
   584	discipline it owes **two** probes.  "Not silently stronger" is discharged by
   585	`thetaSpan_mul_thetaInvSpan_le_one`: the automatic half is landed, so the content is exactly
   586	the reverse inclusion, the same content as chart-typed.
   587	
   588	The mirror risk is **unsatisfiability** — a `Prop` no widened cover can ever satisfy would make
   589	every consumer of it a vacuous theorem, which passes every `sorry` census and axiom probe.  The
   590	probe below rules that out with an unconditional witness, so the residue is genuinely open
   591	rather than false. -/
   592	
   593	/-- **THE SATISFIABILITY PROBE, DISCHARGED at the trivial twist.**  At `a = 0` the theta
   594	cocycle is `1`, so every `thetaOvlUnit` is `1`, both spans are the equalizer algebra itself, and
   595	the pairing holds **unconditionally** — for every widened cover, every adaptation and every
   596	chart typing.
   597	
   598	This does not make the pairing easy at `a > 0`: the content there is the manufactured sections,
   599	which is the open obligation. What it establishes is that `IsThetaPaired` is *satisfiable*, i.e.
   600	that the widened statement is not a reduction to a false hypothesis. -/
   601	theorem isThetaPaired_zero : IsThetaPaired A τ 0 := by
   602	  refine isThetaPaired_of_one_mem A τ 0 ?_
   603	  -- at the trivial twist both spans contain `1`
   604	  have hone : (1 : A.chartProd) ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A (thetaOvlUnit τ 0) := by
   605	    rw [mem_unitGluedSubmodule_iff]
   606	    intro p
   607	    rw [thetaOvlUnit_zero τ p.1 p.2]
   608	    rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, map_one, map_one, Units.val_one, map_one, mul_one]
   609	  have hinvunit : (thetaOvlUnit τ 0)⁻¹
   610	      = (thetaOvlUnit τ 0 : ∀ i j : D.index,
   611	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)ˣ) := by
   612	    funext i j
   613	    rw [Pi.inv_apply, Pi.inv_apply, thetaOvlUnit_zero τ i j, inv_one]
   614	  have hinv : (1 : A.chartProd) ∈ unitGluedSubmodule A (thetaOvlUnit τ 0)⁻¹ := by
   615	    rw [hinvunit]; exact hone
   616	  have := Submodule.mul_mem_mul (mem_thetaSpan_iff A τ 0 |>.mpr hone)
   617	    (mem_thetaInvSpan_iff A τ 0 |>.mpr hinv)
   618	  rwa [one_mul] at this
   619	
   620	end Pairing

   630	/-- **NO `ChartTyping` EXISTS ON A COVER WITH A STRADDLING PIECE.**  If one piece contains a
   631	point outside `V₀` *and* a point outside `V₁`, then `ChartTyping C R π D` is empty: the piece is
   632	assigned some side, `piece_le` puts the *whole* piece inside that pinned chart, and each witness
   633	contradicts one of the two options.
   634	
   635	**This is the honest limit of the whole module, and it cuts against the headline.**  The claim
   636	this file was built on is that the widened carrier lacked a Θ-layer and that supplying it lets
   637	cert-r2's producer reach U2.  The first half stands (see the module docstring's measurements,
   638	independently confirmed as `I-0780`).  The second half does **not**: cert-r2's producer runs
   639	through a cover in which the support sits inside **one** piece `W`
   640	(`exists_affCoverData_swallowedBy`), while the straddling hypotheses of
   641	`forall_not_isCertified_of_straddling` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffStrict.lean:127`) say precisely
   642	that the support has a point outside `V₀` and a point outside `V₁` — and both then lie in `W`.
   643	So on exactly the divisors protection `I-0492`'s widening exists to handle, this file's index
   644	type is uninhabited and every theorem in it is vacuous.
   645	
   646	**Compounding it** (`I-0782`): the tree's only producer of a `ChartTyping` is
   647	`FinCoverData.toChartTyping` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean:255`), the migration *from* the
   648	old chart-typed carrier. So every instantiation available today factors through `FinCoverData`,
   649	i.e. this layer currently computes on the covers the chart-typed layer already handled,

   653	keeps `ChartTyping` separate from the certificate clauses so that a certificate never *requires*

   655	what is **inhabited**. Those are different questions, and only the second one decides whether a
   656	layer indexed by that datum is usable. The recorded shape is `isolating-a-residue-as-a-class`:
   657	check inhabitation of an index before pricing anything stated over it. -/
   658	theorem isEmpty_chartTyping_of_straddling (D : AffCoverData C R) (j : D.index)

   661	    (hy₁ : y ∉ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))) :

     9	# Base change of kernels and regular elements from flat cokernels (the `lm:ctn`-lite home)
    10	
    11	Pure module algebra (no schemes), the shared Tor-lemma home of the DAT-D/DAT-A lanes
    12	(`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §2; Kleiman `lm:ctn`, tex 1747–1815, made cheap by carrying
    13	flatness as data). Everything here is applications of mathlib's purity gift
    14	`LinearMap.lTensor_injective_of_exact_of_flat` (a short exact sequence with flat last
    15	term stays left-exact under any `⊗`).
    16	
    17	For a linear map `δ : M →ₗ[R] N` whose two cokernels are flat — `M ⧸ ker δ` (≅ the
    18	image) and `N ⧸ range δ` — the kernel of `δ` commutes with arbitrary base change:
    19	
    20	* `LinearMap.ker_lTensor_eq_of_flat_coker`: `ker (δ ⊗ A) = range ((ker δ).subtype ⊗ A)`
    21	  for every module `A` (with the `Function.Exact` form
    22	  `LinearMap.exact_lTensor_of_flat_coker`);
    23	* `LinearMap.tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker` /
    24	  `LinearMap.tensorKerEquivOfFlatCoker`: the canonical comparison map
    25	  `LinearMap.tensorKer` — the SAME map as mathlib's flat-base-change case
    26	  `LinearMap.tensorKerEquiv`, so downstream sees one seam with two sufficient
    27	  conditions — is an isomorphism `R' ⊗[R] ker δ ≃ₗ[R'] ker (𝟙 ⊗ δ)`. The DD-1
    28	  certificate consumes this on the glued colength module `W(d) = ker (δ⁻ − δ⁺)`, whose
    29	  certificate clauses (c3)/(c4) are exactly the two flatness hypotheses.
    30	* `Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_flat_coker`: a regular
    31	  element `f ∈ B⁰` of an `R`-algebra with `B ⧸ (f)` flat over `R` stays regular in
    32	  `R' ⊗[R] B` for every `R`-algebra `R'` — the DD-1a `hreg` discharge and the shape
    33	  shared with DAT-A2's germ-regularity bridge (one home, no duplication; DAT-A2's
    34	  fibrewise⟹relative direction is also welcome in this file).
    35	-/

    52	/-- **Purity of the kernel from a flat image**: if `M ⧸ ker δ` is `R`-flat, then the
    53	inclusion of `ker δ` stays injective after tensoring with any module. -/
    54	theorem lTensor_ker_subtype_injective_of_flat_coker
    55	    [Module.Flat R (M ⧸ LinearMap.ker δ)]
    56	    (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
    57	    Function.Injective ((LinearMap.ker δ).subtype.lTensor A) :=
    58	  lTensor_injective_of_exact_of_flat (LinearMap.ker δ).mkQ
    59	    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _) (LinearMap.ker δ).subtype
    60	    (Submodule.injective_subtype _) (exact_subtype_mkQ _) A
    61	
    62	/-- The map `M ⧸ ker δ → N` induced by `δ`. -/
    63	private noncomputable def barMap : M ⧸ LinearMap.ker δ →ₗ[R] N :=
    64	  (LinearMap.ker δ).liftQ δ le_rfl
    65	
    66	private lemma barMap_injective : Function.Injective (barMap δ) := by
    67	  rw [← LinearMap.ker_eq_bot, barMap, Submodule.ker_liftQ]
    68	  simp
    69	
    70	private lemma barMap_comp_mkQ : (barMap δ).comp (LinearMap.ker δ).mkQ = δ :=
    71	  Submodule.liftQ_mkQ _ _ _
    72	
    73	/-- **Purity of the image from a flat cokernel**: if `N ⧸ range δ` is `R`-flat, then
    74	the induced injection `M ⧸ ker δ → N` stays injective after tensoring with any
    75	module. -/
    76	private theorem lTensor_barMap_injective_of_flat_coker
    77	    [Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range δ)]
    78	    (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
    79	    Function.Injective ((barMap δ).lTensor A) := by
    80	  refine lTensor_injective_of_exact_of_flat (LinearMap.range δ).mkQ
    81	    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _) (barMap δ) (barMap_injective δ) ?_ A
    82	  rw [LinearMap.exact_iff, Submodule.ker_mkQ, barMap, Submodule.range_liftQ]
    83	
    84	/-- **Kernel base change from flat cokernels** (the `lm:ctn`-lite keystone, plain
    85	`lTensor` form): if both `M ⧸ ker δ` and `N ⧸ range δ` are `R`-flat, then for any
    86	module `A`, `ker (δ ⊗ A) = range ((ker δ).subtype ⊗ A)`. -/
    87	theorem ker_lTensor_eq_of_flat_coker
    88	    [Module.Flat R (M ⧸ LinearMap.ker δ)] [Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range δ)]
    89	    (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
    90	    LinearMap.ker (δ.lTensor A)
    91	      = LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker δ).subtype.lTensor A) := by
    92	  have hcomp : δ.lTensor A
    93	      = ((barMap δ).lTensor A).comp ((LinearMap.ker δ).mkQ.lTensor A) := by
    94	    rw [← LinearMap.lTensor_comp, barMap_comp_mkQ]
    95	  have hex : Function.Exact ((LinearMap.ker δ).subtype.lTensor A)
    96	      ((LinearMap.ker δ).mkQ.lTensor A) :=
    97	    lTensor_exact A (exact_subtype_mkQ _) (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
    98	  rw [hcomp, LinearMap.ker_comp,
    99	    LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mpr (lTensor_barMap_injective_of_flat_coker δ A),
   100	    Submodule.comap_bot, LinearMap.exact_iff.mp hex]
   101	
   102	variable {δ} in
   103	/-- `ker_lTensor_eq_of_flat_coker` in `Function.Exact` form. -/
   104	theorem exact_lTensor_of_flat_coker
   105	    [Module.Flat R (M ⧸ LinearMap.ker δ)] [Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range δ)]
   106	    (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
   107	    Function.Exact ((LinearMap.ker δ).subtype.lTensor A) (δ.lTensor A) := by
   108	  rw [LinearMap.exact_iff]
   109	  exact ker_lTensor_eq_of_flat_coker δ A

   111	variable (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R']
   112	
   113	/-- **Kernel base change from flat cokernels, comparison form**: the canonical map
   114	`LinearMap.tensorKer : R' ⊗[R] ker δ →ₗ[R'] ker (𝟙 ⊗ δ)` — the same comparison map as
   115	mathlib's flat-base-change `LinearMap.tensorKerEquiv` — is bijective as soon as the two
   116	cokernels of `δ` are flat (no hypothesis on `R'` at all). -/
   117	theorem tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker
   118	    [Module.Flat R (M ⧸ LinearMap.ker δ)] [Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range δ)] :
   119	    Function.Bijective (LinearMap.tensorKer R' R' δ) := by
   120	  constructor
   121	  · intro x y hxy
   122	    have hcoe := congrArg Subtype.val hxy
   123	    rw [LinearMap.tensorKer_coe, LinearMap.tensorKer_coe] at hcoe
   124	    exact lTensor_ker_subtype_injective_of_flat_coker δ R' hcoe
   125	  · rintro ⟨z, hz⟩
   126	    have hz' : z ∈ LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker δ).subtype.lTensor R') := by
   127	      rw [← ker_lTensor_eq_of_flat_coker δ R']
   128	      exact hz
   129	    obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := hz'
   130	    exact ⟨w, Subtype.ext (by rw [LinearMap.tensorKer_coe, hw])⟩
   131	
   132	/-- `tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker`, packaged as a linear equivalence
   133	`R' ⊗[R] ker δ ≃ₗ[R'] ker (𝟙 ⊗ δ)`. -/
   134	noncomputable def tensorKerEquivOfFlatCoker
   135	    [Module.Flat R (M ⧸ LinearMap.ker δ)] [Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range δ)] :
   136	    R' ⊗[R] (LinearMap.ker δ) ≃ₗ[R']
   137	      LinearMap.ker (AlgebraTensorModule.lTensor R' R' δ) :=
   138	  LinearEquiv.ofBijective (LinearMap.tensorKer R' R' δ)
   139	    (tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker δ R')
   140	
   141	@[simp]
   142	theorem tensorKerEquivOfFlatCoker_apply
   143	    [Module.Flat R (M ⧸ LinearMap.ker δ)] [Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range δ)]
   144	    (x : R' ⊗[R] (LinearMap.ker δ)) :
   145	    tensorKerEquivOfFlatCoker δ R' x = LinearMap.tensorKer R' R' δ x :=
   146	  rfl

    48	/-- Kernel spanning after base change is equivalent to injectivity after first
    49	dividing the source by the global kernel.  This is pure linear algebra and holds
    50	for an arbitrary coefficient module `A`.
    51	
    52	The forward direction lifts through the right-exact base change of the quotient
    53	map.  The reverse direction observes that an element in the fibre kernel has zero
    54	image in the fibre of the injectivization, hence already lies in the fibre image
    55	of the global kernel. -/
    56	theorem ker_rTensor_le_range_subtype_iff_liftQ_rTensor_injective
    57	    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
    58	    LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor A) ≤
    59	        LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker f).subtype.rTensor A) ↔
    60	      Function.Injective
    61	        (((LinearMap.ker f).liftQ f le_rfl).rTensor A) := by
    62	  let L := LinearMap.ker f
    63	  have hcomp : f.rTensor A =
    64	      (L.liftQ f le_rfl).rTensor A ∘ₗ L.mkQ.rTensor A := by
    65	    rw [← LinearMap.rTensor_comp, Submodule.liftQ_mkQ]
    66	  have hexact : Function.Exact (L.subtype.rTensor A) (L.mkQ.rTensor A) :=
    67	    rTensor_exact A (LinearMap.exact_subtype_mkQ L) (Submodule.mkQ_surjective L)
    68	  constructor
    69	  · intro hspan
    70	    rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
    71	    intro w hw
    72	    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := LinearMap.rTensor_surjective A
    73	      (Submodule.mkQ_surjective L) w
    74	    have hfx : f.rTensor A x = 0 := by
    75	      rw [hcomp, LinearMap.comp_apply]
    76	      exact hw
    77	    have hx := hspan (LinearMap.mem_ker.mpr hfx)
    78	    rw [← LinearMap.exact_iff.mp hexact, LinearMap.mem_ker] at hx
    79	    exact hx
    80	  · intro hinj x hx
    81	    have hzero : L.mkQ.rTensor A x = 0 := by
    82	      apply hinj
    83	      rw [map_zero]
    84	      have hfx := LinearMap.mem_ker.mp hx
    85	      rw [hcomp, LinearMap.comp_apply] at hfx
    86	      exact hfx
    87	    rw [← LinearMap.exact_iff.mp hexact, LinearMap.mem_ker]
    88	    exact hzero

    92	/-- An independent boundary presentation of every base-changed kernel makes
    93	the injectivized map remain injective after that base change.  This is the
    94	non-circular bridge from a fibrewise Koszul theorem to the relative flatness
    95	criterion: no flatness of the cokernel is assumed.
    96	
    97	The proof lifts through the right-exact base change of `ker(f).mkQ`.  A lift
    98	in the fibre kernel is a base-changed boundary by `hspan`, and the global
    99	identity `f ∘ d = 0` makes its quotient class vanish. -/
   100	theorem liftQ_baseChange_injective_of_boundary
   101	    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (d : P →ₗ[R] M) (hfd : f.comp d = 0)
   102	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
   103	    (hspan : LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.baseChange S f) ≤
   104	      LinearMap.range (LinearMap.baseChange S d)) :
   105	    Function.Injective
   106	      (LinearMap.baseChange S ((LinearMap.ker f).liftQ f le_rfl)) := by
   107	  let L := LinearMap.ker f
   108	  let fbar := L.liftQ f le_rfl
   109	  have hfcomp : LinearMap.baseChange S f =
   110	      (LinearMap.baseChange S fbar).comp (LinearMap.baseChange S L.mkQ) := by
   111	    rw [← LinearMap.baseChange_comp, Submodule.liftQ_mkQ]
   112	  have hdL : ∀ y : P, d y ∈ L := by
   113	    intro y
   114	    apply LinearMap.mem_ker.mpr
   115	    have hy := LinearMap.congr_fun hfd y
   116	    simpa only [LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.zero_apply] using hy
   117	  have hqd : L.mkQ.comp d = 0 := by
   118	    apply LinearMap.ext
   119	    intro y
   120	    rw [LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.zero_apply, Submodule.mkQ_apply,
   121	      Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
   122	    exact hdL y
   123	  rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
   124	  intro w hw
   125	  obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := LinearMap.baseChange_surjective S
   126	    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective L) w
   127	  have hfx : LinearMap.baseChange S f x = 0 := by
   128	    rw [hfcomp, LinearMap.comp_apply]
   129	    exact hw
   130	  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hspan (LinearMap.mem_ker.mpr hfx)
   131	  rw [← hy, ← LinearMap.comp_apply, ← LinearMap.baseChange_comp, hqd,
   132	    LinearMap.baseChange_zero, LinearMap.zero_apply]

    (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    {a : ℕ} (ha1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k π (relThetaCocycle C k π a)).H1)
    (hMa : windowM_choice π hπ g ≤ a) :
    Function.Surjective
      (hc.thetaIdealCokernelToIntrinsic C R π hπ hO hχ ha1 hMa) := by
  let hB := Classical.choose_spec
    (hc.exists_chartAdaptation_subsingleton_thetaIdealH1 C R π hπ hO hχ ha1 hMa)
  let B := Classical.choose
    (hc.exists_chartAdaptation_subsingleton_thetaIdealH1 C R π hπ hO hχ ha1 hMa)

theorem IsCertified.range_thetaIdealCokernelToIntrinsic
    {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    {A : AffAdaptation D d} {g : ℕ} (hc : A.IsCertified g)
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    {a : ℕ} (ha1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k π (relThetaCocycle C k π a)).H1)

    LinearMap.range
        (hc.thetaIdealCokernelToIntrinsic C R π hπ hO hχ ha1 hMa) =
      LinearMap.range (A.intrinsicThetaEvalRel (π := π) a) := by

  change LinearMap.range ((Submodule.subtype _).comp e.toLinearMap) = _

  · intro hy

    exact congrArg Subtype.val (e.apply_symm_apply ⟨y, hy⟩)

The epsilon-identity's consumption of IsCertified really is only three Zariski-local projections, and it can be re-proved from IsLocallyCertified by a squeeze argument — but IsLocallyCertified fails for exactly the divisors IsCertified fails for, because the no-go is about PRODUCING a certificate for a chart-crossing connected divisor and supportLocus is DivEq-invariant and shrink-stable (DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean:30-31 says this verbatim).    183	              _ = s • ((b • (1 : S ⊗[R] A)) ⊗ₜ[A] m) := by

   228	/-- **Finiteness transfer**: an invertible module over a module-finite `R`-algebra is a
   229	finite `R`-module. -/
   230	theorem finite_trans [Module.Finite R A] [Module.Invertible A M] :

   234	/-- **Projectivity transfer**: an invertible module over an `R`-algebra that is
   235	projective as an `R`-module is projective over `R`. -/

   250	/-- (Implementation) The fibre algebra `κ(p) ⊗[R] A` of a finite `R`-algebra is
   251	semilocal: it is a finite algebra over the residue field, hence artinian. -/
   252	theorem finite_maximalSpectrum_fiber (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
   253	    Finite (MaximalSpectrum (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[R] A)) := by
   254	  haveI : IsArtinianRing (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[R] A) := by
   255	    haveI : IsArtinian p.asIdeal.ResidueField (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[R] A) :=
   256	      isArtinian_of_fg_of_artinian'
   257	    exact isArtinian_of_tower p.asIdeal.ResidueField inferInstance
   258	  infer_instance

   260	/-- **The rank transfer** (the semilocal Pic-vanishing): an invertible module over a
   261	finite projective `R`-algebra `A` has the same rank as `A` at every prime of `R`.
   262	Route: `rankAtStalk` is the fibre dimension (`Module.rankAtStalk_eq`); the fibre
   263	`κ(p) ⊗[R] M ≃ (κ(p) ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M` is an invertible module over the fibre algebra,
   264	which is artinian (hence semilocal), so its Picard group is trivial and the fibre is
   265	free of rank one over the fibre algebra. -/
   266	theorem rankAtStalk_eq_of_module_finite (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
   267	    Module.rankAtStalk M p = Module.rankAtStalk A p := by
   268	  haveI : Module.Finite R M := finite_trans (A := A)
   269	  haveI : Module.Projective R M := projective_trans (A := A)
   270	  haveI : Module.Flat R M := Module.Flat.of_projective
   271	  haveI : Module.Flat R A := Module.Flat.of_projective
   272	  rw [Module.rankAtStalk_eq, Module.rankAtStalk_eq]
   273	  set κ := p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   274	  -- the fibre algebra and the fibre of `M` over it
   275	  set Aκ := κ ⊗[R] A with hAκ
   276	  haveI : Finite (MaximalSpectrum Aκ) := finite_maximalSpectrum_fiber (A := A) p
   277	  -- the fibre of `M` as a base change over `A`, an invertible `Aκ`-module
   278	  haveI hinv : Module.Invertible Aκ (Aκ ⊗[A] M) := inferInstance
   279	  haveI : Module.Free Aκ (Aκ ⊗[A] M) := inferInstance
   280	  obtain ⟨e⟩ : Nonempty ((Aκ ⊗[A] M) ≃ₗ[Aκ] Aκ) :=
   281	    Module.Invertible.free_iff_linearEquiv.mp ‹_›
   282	  -- transport dimensions along the collapse and the rank-one equivalence
   283	  have h1 : Module.finrank κ (κ ⊗[R] M) = Module.finrank κ (Aκ ⊗[A] M) :=
   284	    (TensorProduct.baseChangeAlgebraModule κ A M).symm.finrank_eq
   285	  have h2 : Module.finrank κ (Aκ ⊗[A] M) = Module.finrank κ Aκ :=
   286	    (e.restrictScalars κ).finrank_eq
   287	  change Module.finrank κ (κ ⊗[R] M) = Module.finrank κ (κ ⊗[R] A)
   288	  rw [h1, h2]

    11	/-!
    12	# Intrinsic theta descent on a widened divisor cover
    13	
    14	For an arbitrary affine piece `U_j`, the restriction of `O(a Theta)` to the divisor is
    15	the genuine module
    16	
    17	`Gamma(U_j, O(a Theta)) / (f_j) Gamma(U_j, O(a Theta))`.
    18	
    19	Unlike the older chart-typed theta module, this quotient does not choose a trivialization
    20	of the line bundle on `U_j`.  Restriction to `U_i inter U_j` sends the equation-generated
    21	submodule into the symmetric overlap ideal, so the piece quotients have two canonical
    22	overlap maps.  Their equalizer is the intrinsic theta restriction on the widened divisor.
    23	
    24	The construction below supplies the module that the widened equalizer algebra acts on.
    25	It is the chart-free input for proving invertibility and identifying the result with the
    26	cover-independent high-window quotient.
    27	-/

   230	theorem thetaSectionsToOverlapLeft_vanishing_le (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)

   240	          (A.ThetaOverlapSections (π := π) a i j)))

/-- **`W(d)^{Θᵃ}` is a module over the equalizer algebra** by componentwise
multiplication. -/
noncomputable instance : Module ↥A.gluedSubalgebra (A.ThetaGlued a) :=
  Function.Injective.module ↥A.gluedSubalgebra
    ((A.thetaGluedSubmodule a).subtype.toAddMonoidHom) Subtype.val_injective
    (fun c x => by
      change ((c • x : A.ThetaGlued a) : A.chartProd) = c • (x : A.chartProd)
      rw [smul_thetaGlued_coe, Algebra.smul_def]
      rfl)

instance : IsScalarTower R ↥A.gluedSubalgebra (A.ThetaGlued a) where
  smul_assoc r c x := by
    refine Subtype.ext ?_
    have h1 : (((r • c) • x : A.ThetaGlued a) : A.chartProd)
        = ((r • c : ↥A.gluedSubalgebra) : A.chartProd) * x := rfl
    have h2 : ((r • (c • x) : A.ThetaGlued a) : A.chartProd)
        = r • ((c • x : A.ThetaGlued a) : A.chartProd) := rfl
    have h3 : ((c • x : A.ThetaGlued a) : A.chartProd) = (c : A.chartProd) * x := rfl
    have h4 : ((r • c : ↥A.gluedSubalgebra) : A.chartProd)
        = r • (c : A.chartProd) := rfl
    rw [h1, h2, h3, h4, smul_mul_assoc]

/-- The twisted `A_D`-submodule and `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` have the same carrier,
`A_D`-linearly. -/
noncomputable def thetaSpanEquiv :
    ↥(A.thetaSpan a : Submodule ↥A.gluedSubalgebra A.chartProd)
      ≃ₗ[↥A.gluedSubalgebra] A.ThetaGlued a where
  toFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
  invFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
  map_add' _ _ := rfl
  map_smul' c x := by
    refine Subtype.ext ?_
    rw [smul_thetaGlued_coe]
    change (c • (x : A.chartProd)) = (c : A.chartProd) * x
    rw [Algebra.smul_def]
    rfl
  left_inv _ := rfl
  right_inv _ := rfl

/-- **Invertibility of `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` over the equalizer algebra**, on the consumer's
carrier. -/
theorem invertible_thetaGlued (h : A.IsThetaPaired a) :
    Module.Invertible ↥A.gluedSubalgebra (A.ThetaGlued a) :=
  haveI := A.invertible_thetaSpan a h
  Module.Invertible.congr (A.thetaSpanEquiv a)

/-- **(c2)-transport, finiteness**: under the pairing input, the Θ-twisted glued module
is a finite `R`-module. -/
theorem finite_thetaGlued (h : A.IsThetaPaired a) (hfin : Module.Finite R A.Glued) :
    Module.Finite R (A.ThetaGlued a) := by
  haveI := hfin
  haveI : Module.Finite R ↥A.gluedSubalgebra :=
    Module.Finite.equiv A.gluedSubalgebraEquiv.symm
  haveI := A.invertible_thetaGlued a h
  exact Module.Invertible.finite_trans (A := ↥A.gluedSubalgebra)

/-- **(c2)-transport, projectivity**: under the pairing input, the Θ-twisted glued
module is projective over `R`. -/
theorem projective_thetaGlued (h : A.IsThetaPaired a)
    (hproj : Module.Projective R A.Glued) :
    Module.Projective R (A.ThetaGlued a) := by
  haveI := hproj
  haveI : Module.Projective R ↥A.gluedSubalgebra :=
    Module.Projective.of_equiv A.gluedSubalgebraEquiv.symm
  haveI := A.invertible_thetaGlued a h
  exact Module.Invertible.projective_trans (A := ↥A.gluedSubalgebra)

/-- **(c2)-transport, constant rank** (the semilocal Pic-vanishing): under the pairing
input and the certificate, the Θ-twisted glued module has the same constant fibre rank
`n` as the untwisted one — the input `divisorWindowGr` consumes. -/
theorem rankAtStalk_thetaGlued {n : ℕ} (h : A.IsThetaPaired a) (hc : A.IsCertified n)
    (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
    Module.rankAtStalk (A.ThetaGlued a) p = n := by
  haveI := hc.finite_glued
  haveI := hc.projective_glued
  haveI : Module.Finite R ↥A.gluedSubalgebra :=
    Module.Finite.equiv A.gluedSubalgebraEquiv.symm
  haveI : Module.Projective R ↥A.gluedSubalgebra :=
    Module.Projective.of_equiv A.gluedSubalgebraEquiv.symm
  haveI := A.invertible_thetaGlued a h
  rw [Module.Invertible.rankAtStalk_eq_of_module_finite (A := ↥A.gluedSubalgebra) p,
    congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv A.gluedSubalgebraEquiv) p]
  exact hc.rankAtStalk_glued p

end DivisorAdaptation

end AlgebraicGeometry
/-- Compatible representatives of an intrinsic theta class determine a global section of
the auxiliary theta cokernel whose restriction to every widened piece is their local
cokernel class. -/
theorem exists_thetaCokernel_global_of_compatible_representatives
    {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    {A : AffAdaptation D d} (B : DivisorAdaptation C R π d) (a : ℕ)
    (r : ∀ j : D.index, A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j)
    (hr : ∀ i j : D.index,
      A.thetaToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j (Submodule.Quotient.mk (r i)) =
        A.thetaToOverlapRight (π := π) a i j (Submodule.Quotient.mk (r j))) :
    ∃ q : (cokernel (B.thetaIdealIncl (a := a))).obj.obj
        (op (⊤ : (relCurve C R).Opens)),
      ∀ j : D.index,
        secRes (cokernel (B.thetaIdealIncl (a := a)))
          (le_top : D.pieces j ≤ (⊤ : (relCurve C R).Opens)) q =
          ((cokernel.π (B.thetaIdealIncl (a := a))).hom.app
            (op (D.pieces j))).hom
            (gluedTwistEquiv C R π a (D.pieces j) (r j)) := by
  let Q := cokernel (B.thetaIdealIncl (a := a))
  have hcompat := thetaPieceCokernel_family_isCompatible C R π B a r hr
  have hcover : (⊤ : (relCurve C R).Opens) ≤ ⨆ j : D.index, D.pieces j := by
    rw [D.cover]
  obtain ⟨q, hq, -⟩ := TopCat.Sheaf.existsUnique_gluing'
    Q D.pieces (⊤ : (relCurve C R).Opens)
    (fun j => homOfLE (le_top : D.pieces j ≤ (⊤ : (relCurve C R).Opens)))
    hcover
    (fun j => ((cokernel.π (B.thetaIdealIncl (a := a))).hom.app
      (op (D.pieces j))).hom
      (gluedTwistEquiv C R π a (D.pieces j) (r j)))
    hcompat
  exact ⟨q, hq⟩

/-- Surjectivity of the auxiliary theta-cokernel projection on global sections forces
surjectivity of intrinsic theta evaluation on the arbitrary widened affine cover.  The
proof chooses local quotient representatives, glues their cokernel classes, and uses
piecewise exactness to compare the resulting global lift back to those representatives. -/
theorem intrinsicThetaEvalRel_surjective_of_thetaIdealCokernel_app_top_surjective
    {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    {A : AffAdaptation D d} (B : DivisorAdaptation C R π d) (a : ℕ)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective
      ((cokernel.π (B.thetaIdealIncl (a := a))).hom.app
        (op (⊤ : (relCurve C R).Opens))).hom) :
    Function.Surjective (A.intrinsicThetaEvalRel (π := π) a) := by
  intro y
  choose r hr using fun j : D.index =>
    Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective (A.thetaPieceVanishing (π := π) a j) (y.val j)
  have hcompat : ∀ i j : D.index,
      A.thetaToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j (Submodule.Quotient.mk (r i)) =
        A.thetaToOverlapRight (π := π) a i j (Submodule.Quotient.mk (r j)) := by
    intro i j
    have hy := (A.mem_intrinsicThetaGluedSubmodule_iff (π := π) a y.val).mp
      y.property ⟨i, j⟩
    rw [hr i, hr j]
    exact hy
  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := exists_thetaCokernel_global_of_compatible_representatives
    C R π B a r hcompat
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hsurj q
  refine ⟨x, ?_⟩
  apply Subtype.ext
  funext j
  letI : Module Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)
      (A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a j) :=
    A.thetaPieceSectionsModule (π := π) a j
  change Submodule.Quotient.mk
      (secRes (thetaChartDatum C R π a).sheaf
        (le_top : D.pieces j ≤ (⊤ : (relCurve C R).Opens))
        ((gluedTwistEquiv C R π a (⊤ : (relCurve C R).Opens)).symm x)) =
      y.val j
  rw [← hr j]
  apply thetaPieceQuotient_eq_of_global_cokernel_restriction C R π B a j x (r j)
  calc
    secRes (cokernel (B.thetaIdealIncl (a := a)))
        (le_top : D.pieces j ≤ (⊤ : (relCurve C R).Opens))
        (((cokernel.π (B.thetaIdealIncl (a := a))).hom.app
          (op (⊤ : (relCurve C R).Opens))).hom x) =
      secRes (cokernel (B.thetaIdealIncl (a := a)))
        (le_top : D.pieces j ≤ (⊤ : (relCurve C R).Opens)) q := by
          rw [hx]
    _ = ((cokernel.π (B.thetaIdealIncl (a := a))).hom.app
        (op (D.pieces j))).hom
        (gluedTwistEquiv C R π a (D.pieces j) (r j)) := hq j

end AffAdaptation

variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))]

/-- The widened certificate's global theta-cokernel surjectivity is enough to make the
intrinsic, chart-free theta evaluation surjective. -/
theorem IsCertified.intrinsicThetaEvalRel_surjective
    {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    {A : AffAdaptation D d} {g : ℕ} (hc : A.IsCertified g)
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    {a : ℕ} (ha1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k π (relThetaCocycle C k π a)).H1)
    (hMa : windowM_choice π hπ g ≤ a) :
    Function.Surjective (A.intrinsicThetaEvalRel (π := π) a) := by
  obtain ⟨B, hB⟩ := hc.exists_chartAdaptation_thetaIdealCokernel_app_top_surjective
    C R π hπ hO hχ ha1 hMa
  exact intrinsicThetaEvalRel_surjective_of_thetaIdealCokernel_app_top_surjective
    C R π B a hB

/-- The certified intrinsic high-window carve is surjective. -/
theorem IsCertified.intrinsicWindowCarve_surjective
    {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    {A : AffAdaptation D d} {g : ℕ} (hc : A.IsCertified g)
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    {a : ℕ} (ha1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k π (relThetaCocycle C k π a)).H1)
    (hMa : windowM_choice π hπ g ≤ a) :
    Function.Surjective (A.intrinsicWindowCarve (π := π) a ha1) := by
  rw [intrinsicWindowCarve, LinearMap.coe_comp]
  exact (hc.intrinsicThetaEvalRel_surjective C R π hπ hO hχ ha1 hMa).comp
    (relThetaWindowEquiv C R π a ha1).surjective

/-- The certified intrinsic window quotient is linearly equivalent to the descended
theta restriction, with the established divisor-window kernel and no extra hypothesis. -/
noncomputable def IsCertified.intrinsicWindowQuotEquiv
    {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    {A : AffAdaptation D d} {g : ℕ} (hc : A.IsCertified g)
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    {a : ℕ} (ha1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k π (relThetaCocycle C k π a)).H1)
    (hMa : windowM_choice π hπ g ≤ a) :
    ((R ⊗[k] ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) ⧸
        divisorWindow d ha1) ≃ₗ[R]
      A.IntrinsicThetaGlued (π := π) a :=
  (Submodule.quotEquivOfEq _ _
      (A.ker_intrinsicWindowCarve (π := π) a ha1).symm).trans
    ((A.intrinsicWindowCarve (π := π) a ha1).quotKerEquivOfSurjective
      (hc.intrinsicWindowCarve_surjective C R π hπ hO hχ ha1 hMa))

/-- Once the widened certificate supplies the auxiliary theta-ideal `H¹` vanishing,
global sections of the quotient sheaf for the chosen auxiliary chart are linearly equivalent
to the actual range of the intrinsic widened theta evaluation. -/
noncomputable def IsCertified.thetaIdealCokernelEquivIntrinsicRange
    {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    {A : AffAdaptation D d} {g : ℕ} (hc : A.IsCertified g)
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    {a : ℕ} (ha1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k π (relThetaCocycle C k π a)).H1)
    (hMa : windowM_choice π hπ g ≤ a) :
    let B := Classical.choose
      (hc.exists_chartAdaptation_subsingleton_thetaIdealH1 C R π hπ hO hχ ha1 hMa)
